newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Timorese leave Indonesia for asylum in Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Timorese leave Indonesia for asylum in Portugal.

text.p: Five East Timorese holed up in the Spanish Embassy in Jakarta for two weeks left Indonesia on Tuesday for asylum in Portugal, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said.

The five Timorese men entered the embassy on September 10 and had earlier asked that a statement on human rights issues be broadcast on international radio before they would leave the embassy compound in central Jakarta.
An ICRC official said the five had boarded a Royal Dutch Airlines KLM flight to Amsterdam. "There have been no problems", the official said.
An airline official confirmed the plane left Jakarta's Sukarno-Hatta international airport on time shortly after 7 p.m. (1200 GMT).
A Spanish diplomat earlier told Reuters the five had left for asylum in Portugal.

Portugal is the former colonial power in East Timor, which was invaded by Indonesia in 1975 and annexed the following year in an act not recognised by the United Nations. The U.N. still regards Lisbon as the administering power.
Since September last year, 84 East Timorese have been granted asylum in Portugal after entering foreign embassies in Jakarta. All have had their travel facilitated by the ICRC.
